content: Reference document landed in chronicle archive 2026-05-27: comprehensive synthesis of CBD-induced liver safety literature through May 2026, focused on the gap in mainstream data on transdermal vs oral CBD metabolite ratios and liver outcomes. Sources: Epidiolex FDA label (2025 revision), Florian et al. JAMA Internal Medicine 2025 (the 5 mg/kg lower-dose oral CBD trial showing 5.6% ALT >3x ULN), Watkins et al. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2021, Lo et al. J Intern Med 2023 meta-analysis, Beers et al. Toxicology In Vitro 2025 (3D hepatocyte spheroid CBD+VPA), Zhang et al. Med Cannabis Cannabinoids 2024 (metabolite kinetics in healthy adults), Taylor et al. CNS Drugs 2018 (industry-sponsored PK), Rimmerman 2013 (VDAC1 binding), Perucca and Bialer CNS Drugs 2020 (oral bioavailability ~6%), Zamarripa et al. J Anal Toxicol 2024 (topical metabolite ratios), Heussler 2019 (Fragile X transdermal CBD gel), Charoenporn 2024 (CanPatch psoriasis trial protocol). KEY FINDINGS: (1) oral CBD ALT signal is well-documented and dose-dependent; (2) the 7-COOH-CBD/BSEP mechanism is asserted on the Epidiolex label without published IC50 values, and the hepatocellular-not-cholestatic in vivo phenotype weakens BSEP-inhibition as the primary mechanism; (3) the metabolite-to-parent AUC ratio differs dramatically by route: oral 7-40x, transdermal ~2x, inhaled near-zero; (4) THE SPECIFIC MISSING MEASUREMENT is paired LC-MS/MS metabolite fingerprint plus LFT panels in steady-state transdermal vs oral CBD users, which has not been published as of May 2026 and could discriminate among three competing mechanistic explanations; (5) archived plasma re-assay from prior transdermal bioequivalence work is a plausible low-cost path. NOTABLE EXTENSIONS the document surfaces: CYP2C9*3 polymorphism effects on CBD clearance, 2.45-5.15x AUC increase in hepatic impairment, sex differences in 7-COOH-CBD exposure (~2x higher in females), Validcare observational study limitations (industry funded, low dose, end-point-only LFTs), UK FSA 10 mg/day advisory limit, additional biomarkers worth measuring (CK-18, miR-122, bile acid panel, mtDNA copy number), and mitochondrial-reserve framing connecting back to the two-pathway model. Full document at archive_id 9281572314dcb1a557a7177052d40721bddceac85132d177b491ea2a65399631 (conversation_id cbd_liver_safety_transdermal_gap_2026_05_27, 39851 bytes). PROVENANCE NOTE: this synthesis emerged as a productive divergence from a discussion about a separate two-pathway dose-engagement framework. The divergence revealed the transdermal liver-safety hypothesis as a parallel research surface independent of, but compatible with, the dose-pathway model. Both rest on the same underlying mitochondrial-stress-test mechanism but via different pharmacokinetic gates (route-of-administration vs concentration window).
